title: I’m building a Unity MCP bridge that lets an agent rebuild scenes from a reference image
author: kirby23082010
selftext:
I’ve been experimenting with a Unity MCP bridge focused on the full workflow loop inside the editor: making changes in Unity, inspecting the result, and iterating from visual feedback. This clip shows the workflow: giving the agent a reference image and asking it to rebuild the scene inside Unity. It’s definitely not perfect yet, but I think it’s a promising start.

[Reference image → Unity scene reconstruction](https://i.redd.it/j1a3jh2f4wng1.gif)

I’m less interested in “AI writes some code” and more in whether an agent can handle practical editor tasks in a tighter loop: create/update, compare against the goal, and keep refining.There are already other Unity MCP projects out there, but I wanted to explore my own approach with deeper editor coverage, visual QA, and scene reconstruction workflows.

Open source: [https://github.com/sebastiankurvers-dev/agent-bridge-for-unity](https://github.com/sebastiankurvers-dev/agent-bridge-for-unity)

Would love feedback from anyone exploring AI-native Unity workflows.

comments.author: Otherwise_Wave9374
comments.body: This is a fun approach, reference-image to scene reconstruction is exactly the kind of practical agent task that feels real. If you add a quick eval step (diff against target composition, object counts, lighting) the agent can iterate way more reliably. Ive been keeping a small list of agent eval ideas here: https://www.agentixlabs.com/blog/

replies.author: kirby23082010
replies.body: Thanks! That's already built in — the compare tools return per-channel deltas, luminance/saturation diffs, and hotspot regions with actionable suggestions. There's also convergence tracking that detects when similarity plateaus and tells the agent to stop tweaking or try a different approach. The villa reconstruction GIF is that full loop running end to end.

comments.author: Otherwise_Wave9374
comments.body: This is super cool. The tight edit/inspect/iterate loop is exactly where AI agents feel most useful vs one-shot codegen. Curious how youre handling state + tool feedback (like reading scene graph, lighting params, materials) so the agent can self-correct instead of just retrying. Ive been collecting patterns for agent eval and tool loops lately, a few notes here if useful: https://www.agentixlabs.com/blog/

replies.author: kirby23082010
replies.body: The agent has full read access to the scene graph hierarchy, components, serialized properties, render settings, material properties, volume profiles. So when a compare says "too dark," it can inspect the actual light intensities and adjust specifically rather than guessing. The checkpoint system also lets it snapshot before experimenting and roll back if things get worse.

comments.author: Cubey42
comments.body:
I'm untaking a unity project now using Claude opus, my question is if I switch to your mcp thing, will it be able to look at project files without me having to keep sending them? Does this also benefit just any unity work?
Edit: sorry my question was vague

replies.author: kirby23082010
replies.body: Yes that should work. It can query the scene hierarchy, inspect any GameObject's components and properties, read scripts, search assets, check materials/shaders, read console logs, etc. You don't need to copy-paste anything. It benefits any Unity work, not just scene building. If you're debugging, the agent can read the console, inspect component values, and check render settings on its own. If you're scripting, it can create scripts, wait for compilation, enter Play Mode, and verify the result.

replies.author: Cubey42
replies.body: can it see the game scene? I often do alot of troubleshoot with sending images as well, it helps me with working with Claude

replies.author: kirby23082010
replies.body: Yeah it can capture screenshots from the scene view, game view, or any specific camera. The agent can also compare screenshots against reference images and get back metrics on what's different so instead of you screenshotting and pasting, the agent just takes one itself, looks at it, and adjusts.

replies.author: kirby23082010
replies.body: Sorry, not at the moment. Maybe in the future!
